title: Why You Struggle With Eye Contact More With Strangers
hook: Why does making eye contact with strangers feel so awkward?

narration.text: Holding a stranger's gaze often feels more uncomfortable than looking at a friend.
This is because your brain processes unfamiliar faces as potential threats.
Prolonged eye contact can signal aggression or a challenge in new social situations.
With friends, your brain registers safety and familiarity.
Eye contact then strengthens social bonds and trust, rather than indicating danger.
Notice how your comfort level changes when you meet someone new versus an old acquaintance.
Try it right now and tell me if it worked on you, like this if it surprised you, and subscribe to understand your mind better.

description: Ever wondered why maintaining eye contact with a stranger feels so different from a friend? It is all about how your brain perceives social signals and potential threats. Learn the fascinating psychology behind this everyday interaction.
topic: Why you often feel more uncomfortable holding eye contact with a stranger than a friend. This is about social bonding and threat perception.
